content.title: Data Structures and Algorithms in Java - Multiple Choice Rubric

institution_context.target_students: FPT University students studying data structures and algorithms in Java
course_context: CSD-style algorithmic reasoning and data structure understanding
Assessment should emphasize concept understanding before advanced theory

easy.description: Concept-level questions about one data structure or algorithm idea with direct reasoning.
expected_skills: Recognize array, stack, queue, linked list, tree, graph, sorting, or searching basics.
Identify core properties or direct use cases.

medium.description: Questions requiring moderate reasoning about algorithm behavior, data structure operations, or time-complexity implications.
expected_skills: Trace short operations on a structure.
Reason about ordinary edge cases or operation sequences.
should_avoid: Deep advanced optimizations outside course scope.

hard.description: Questions requiring careful algorithmic reasoning, close comparison of operations, or understanding of subtle data-structure behavior.
expected_skills: Trace non-trivial state changes or operation sequences.
Differentiate between close complexity or structure-behavior options.
Use chunk-grounded algorithmic reasoning rather than simple recall.
should_avoid: Topics not covered by the provided chunks.
Advanced theorem-heavy material outside standard coursework.

review_checks: The question must be grounded in the provided chunks.
The item must target DSA concepts in Java course scope.
Difficulty must match the actual reasoning depth.
Options must be technically meaningful and non-trivial.
correct_answer must match valid option labels.
Explanation must justify the answer with algorithm or structure reasoning.

easy: Requires tracing many operations or states.
Depends on hidden implementation details not present in the chunks.
medium: Only asks for a direct textbook definition.
Requires proof-level reasoning well above standard course scope.
Uses highly advanced optimizations absent from the material.
hard: Can be answered by a single-property recall.
Has obvious distractors with no meaningful trade-off.
Does not require algorithmic or operational reasoning.

acceptance_rules: Accept only if the item is chunk-grounded and DSA-relevant.
Reject if complexity claims or structure behavior are incorrect.
Reject if the stated difficulty does not match the reasoning load.
regeneration_hints: Use direct property checks for Easy items.
Use short traces or operation comparisons for Medium items.
Use nuanced algorithmic reasoning for Hard items.
